title: Disability Compensation Decision Past-Due: Standing Months and Amount Already Paid
content:
**Definition of the amount.** The decision past-due on a Disability Compensation award is the monthly entitlement the decisions support for the months with a standing monthly payment, less what stands paid toward it, and never less than nothing; it is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Standing months.** A month has a standing monthly payment when a monthly payment was issued for it and did not come back, or came back and was replaced. Their number is the monthly payments issued, less those that came back, plus the replacements.

**What stands paid.** What stands paid toward a decision past-due is the gross of every monthly payment issued, less the gross of every payment that came back, plus the gross of every replacement and of every past-due release already on the award.

**Monthly entitlement.** The monthly entitlement for a decision past-due is the veteran-alone rate of the award's combined rating for each standing month — the rate the Disability Compensation rate table gives for the tier the award now carries.

**Worked example (hypothetical award now at Disability Compensation (70% Combined Rating)).**

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Monthly payments issued | 7, each with a gross of 1435.02 |
| Payments that came back | 1 (gross 1435.02), replaced once (gross 1435.02) |
| Standing months | 7 less 1 plus 1, that is 7 |
| Entitlement the decisions support | 1808.45 multiplied by 7, that is 12659.15 |
| What stands paid | 10045.14 less 1435.02 plus 1435.02, no earlier release, that is 10045.14 |
| Decision past-due | 12659.15 less 10045.14, that is 2614.01 |

**Floor.** Where what stands paid exceeds the entitlement for the standing months, the decision past-due is nothing; it is never a negative figure.
